title: token-misrouting-429-throttling-spike-root-cause-and-mitigation
creator: Aisha Raman
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 a burst of 429s was observed across multiple customer routes. Investigation showed quota counters were being applied to incorrect tenant buckets due to an auth header normalization mismatch between edge proxies and the rate-limiter service. The misrouting caused cascading throttling and automated client retries produced a thundering-429 effect across our gateway cluster.
timeline:
2026-03-09 09:12 UTC - First alert: spike in 429 rate on gateway-prod
2026-03-09 09:18 UTC - SRE paged; initial mitigation: increased worker pool and opened emergency circuit breaker for noisy route
2026-03-09 09:27 UTC - Logs show repeated token canonicalization failures at edge-proxy->auth-adapter boundary; some requests carried legacy 'Authorization' casing and others had trimmed whitespace
2026-03-09 09:40 UTC - Rate-limiter returned tenant-id fallback to 'unknown' which maps to a low-capacity quota; this caused immediate local over-quota responses
2026-03-09 09:55 UTC - Traffic engineering routed affected tenants to dedicated backends temporarily; rate of 429s subsided by 10:20 UTC
2026-03-09 11:00 UTC - Hotfix deployed to normalize headers in edge-proxy and add strict validation; follow-up plan drafted
root_causes: 1) Header canonicalization mismatch: edge proxy trimmed trailing characters while auth-adapter expected exact header formatting. 2) Rate-limiter fallback semantics: when tenant lookup failed it used a global low-capacity bucket instead of rejecting or falling back to more permissive policy. 3) Insufficient telemetry on tenant-mapping failures; alarms were on token validation errors but not on tenant mapping fallthroughs. 4) Client retry behavior + lack of coordinated retry backoff led to amplification.
impact: High. ~18% of customer requests for 12 tenants returned 429s during the spike window. Several engineering customers reported degraded product experience and one enterprise customer opened a support escalation. No data loss, but SLO breaches for 3 routes and billing disputes for overage-like errors expected.
investigation_notes:
- Correlated traces show the majority of misrouted tokens had non-UTF8 padded characters introduced by older SDKs.
- Auth-adapter used a legacy header lookup map that was not in sync with edge-proxy's normalization rules (PR review gap).
- Rate-limiter mapping logic prioritized 'mapped tenant id' then fell back to global unknown bucket with capacity 10rps; this choice was historical from pre-multi-tenant rollout.
- Canary logs indicate the header normalization change in edge-proxy deployed two weeks prior increased token variance but passed unit tests because tests used canonical headers only.
- Reproduced locally by sending Authorization header variants; observed tenant resolution divergence in 40% of cases for malformed tokens.
action_items: ENG-11022: Fix auth-adapter header parsing to accept trimmed and padded headers and add normalization module (owner: Marco Varela, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-11023: Change rate-limiter fallback behavior: reject with 401/400 on tenant-lookup failure instead of assigning unknown low-capacity bucket (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG-11024: Add explicit alert 'tenant-lookup-fallback-rate > 0.5% of requests' to gateway SLOs and on-call playbook (owner: Oncall Team, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-11025: Implement short-lived coordinated retry-backoff header (Retry-After) and educate SDK teams to honour exponential backoff (owner: SDK Team, due: 2026-04-01)
ENG-11026: Add end-to-end fuzz tests for Authorization header variants in CI and include a tenant-mapping validation test (owner: QA, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-11027: Run a capacity exercise to evaluate dedicated buckets for high-volume enterprise tenants to avoid cross-tenant noise (owner: Infra Capacity, due: 2026-04-05)
ENG-11028: Update runbook and create a post-incident customer communication template for quota-related 429 storms (owner: SRE/Support, due: 2026-03-16)
ENG-11029: Backfill logs for tenant resolution decisions for the past 30 days and surface a dashboard for 'tenant-mapping errors' (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-20)
notes_for_customers: We identified a header normalization mismatch that caused some tokens to be misattributed to an internal low-capacity bucket, producing 429 responses for a subset of tenants. A targeted fix and improved validation are deployed; full mitigations and SDK guidance are scheduled. Support will follow up with affected customers directly.
